parts.instructions: Write a word from the box in the correct form in each gap. Box: benefit · debt · dividend · insurance · interest · investment · mortgage · overdraft · pension · share

passages.title: Money management – an introduction
passages.text:
Different bank accounts pay different amounts of (1) ____. It makes sense to shop around before you open an account.
If your salary doesn't always get you to the end of the month, you'll have to arrange a/an (2) ____ with your bank, so it's worth being on good terms with your bank manager.
If you're planning to buy a house, you'll probably need to get a/an (3) ____. Once again, shop around to get the best deal.
If you're thinking about taking out life (4) ____, make sure you talk to an independent financial advisor. They'll give you unbiased advice.
Make sure you know what (5) ____ you're entitled to. If you're on a low income and have a family, you may be surprised how much you'll receive from the state each month.
Even if you're only in your early twenties, it pays to plan for the future. If you can, start paying into a/an (6) ____ scheme now to ensure you have a comfortable retirement.
It goes without saying that you should try to avoid getting into too much (7) ____. Only buy things on credit if you're sure you can afford to pay the monthly instalments.
If you do manage to start saving a little each month, you might want to think about buying some (8) ____. Their value can go down of course, but they can be a good (9) ____, particularly in the mid- to long-term. Many companies pay an annual (10) ____ to shareholders – this can be a welcome source of extra income if the company's doing well.

items.stem: Different bank accounts pay different amounts of ____.
items.explanation_vi: Tài khoản ngân hàng trả lãi (interest).

items.stem: If your salary doesn't always get you to the end of the month, you'll have to arrange a/an ____ with your bank.
items.explanation_vi: Overdraft là thấu chi, được rút quá số dư.

items.stem: If you're planning to buy a house, you'll probably need to get a/an ____.
items.explanation_vi: Mortgage là khoản vay thế chấp mua nhà.

items.stem: If you're thinking about taking out life ____, make sure you talk to an independent financial advisor.
items.explanation_vi: Life insurance là bảo hiểm nhân thọ.

items.stem: Make sure you know what ____ you're entitled to.
items.explanation_vi: Benefits là các khoản trợ cấp nhà nước.

items.stem: If you can, start paying into a/an ____ scheme now to ensure you have a comfortable retirement.
items.explanation_vi: Pension scheme là quỹ hưu trí.

items.stem: It goes without saying that you should try to avoid getting into too much ____.
items.explanation_vi: Get into debt là mắc nợ.

items.stem: If you do manage to start saving a little each month, you might want to think about buying some ____.
Their value can go down of course, but they can be a good ____, particularly in the mid- to long-term.
Many companies pay an annual ____ to shareholders.
items.explanation_vi: Dividend là cổ tức chia cho cổ đông.
